content:
alex: Kicking off an RFC draft for an SLO-driven routing + prefetch policy. wanted to get alignment before i lock scope.

maria: nice. is this primarily about choosing runtime kernels or more about where requests land (hot vs cold pools)?

alex: both. idea is a policy layer that routes by predicted tail latency risk and can trigger prefetching of KV entries or lighter kernels. goal: hit 95th p99 latency SLOs without blowing cost.

sam: customer ask from FinTech X was exactly this — they want low tail latency for short prompts but don't want heavy kernels for all traffic.

jen: keep scope minimal for v1. proposal: 1) routing decision service (latency score) 2) prefetch API for KV cache 3) simple fallback policy. no fancy learns.

alex: agreed. v1 acceptance criteria proposal:
- end-to-end p95/p99 telemetry per route and model variant available in console
- when predicted tail risk > threshold, route to low-latency variant or prefetch KV within 10ms decision window
- prefetch should be opt-in per route and revertible (canary + kill switch)

nate: what's the prediction signal? Heuristics on seq_len + recent latency + token distribution?

alex: MVP: short heuristic: seq_len histogram + recent 1m latency tail. we can add ML scorer in v2.

lisa: edge case: batched requests where prefix matches partially — prefetch could worsen throughput. need acceptance criteria about throughput degradation (<=5% drop at 95th perc).

sam: also consider memory pressure on GPU with aggressive prefetching. define guard rails (max prefetched keys per GPU).

jen: +1. propose a circuit breaker: if GPU mem pressure > 80% then prefetch disabled for that instance. add to RFC.

alex: draft PRD sections i'm planning: motivation, customer signals, non-goals, API surface (route config + prefetch flags), runtime hooks, metrics, rollout plan, acceptance tests.

maria: rollout plan should include: alpha on Dedicated, smoke on Hosted (low traffic orgs), A/B compare tokens/cost for 2 weeks, automated regression alerts on quality.

ci-bot: RFC doc created: https://redwood-internal/docs/rfcs/slo-routing-prefetch (draft) :page_facing_up:

alex: please review the doc and leave comments inline. open q: do we want an explicit quantization-aware kernel preference in v1 or leave kernel selection untouched?

sam: leave kernel selection for separate kernel-selection RFC. this one's orchestration/policy focused.

lisa: acceptance test idea: synthetic traffic mix (short chat + long generation) run for 24h with and without policy; verify p99 improves and cost delta within target. include script in repo.

jen: scope negotiation note: if we add ML predictor it becomes a cross-team project with infra/research. mark as v2.

maria: i can lobby customer success to find two customers for alpha. will add to the doc.

alex: awesome. i'll push a more fleshed draft by EOD. tagging folks: @maria @sam @jen for early review.

nate: quick nit — add a section with explicit fallback ordering: 1) route to low-latency variant, 2) attempt KV prefetch, 3) fall back to smaller model.

alex: added. thanks.

sam: cool. will test the simulation harness tomorrow and report perf numbers here. :rocket:
